legacy_root.answer: On 8 fixture cases the Claude vs Codex canonical request-diff is empty for 4 portable cases ['cv-p-01', 'cv-p-02', 'cv-p-03', 'cv-p-04'] and non-empty for 4 leak cases ['cv-timeout-clamp', 'cv-claude-task', 'cv-codex-mcp', 'cv-webfetch-vs-search']. Codex clamps timeout 300s→180s on cv-timeout-clamp (canonical timeout differs, so the case is excluded from scoring). Claude-only Task and WebFetch, and Codex-only mcp__codex__codex, return typed UNSUPPORTED with score=null rather than a FAIL. The silent-fallback mutant drops the missing tool and scores 0.0, which the degrade detector catches. Scores on the empty-diff subset are identical (oracle 1.0/1.0). Encoding leaks (inline vs prompt-file transport; Read vs shell native names) are listed separately and do not by themselves empty the score subset. Catalog input command-center/bench/cases/ is unbuilt (dependency TST-0295); this unit runs a closed fixture slice rather than live vendor calls. SUCCESS:TST-0316

legacy_root.question: Question: the same case set run through the Claude adapter and the Codex adapter should differ in RESULT, not in what was actually asked. Diff the effective request each adapter builds (prompt, tools offered, context assembled, timeout) and report every divergence, then run the parity benchmark. Spec :10983 forbids pretending full interchangeability where tools, context or permissions differ and requires degrading loudly; this unit produces the concrete list of what actually differs.
legacy_root.title: Cross-vendor benchmark parity, and the abstraction leaks it exposes
